faqLeft.q: What engine does the Mercedes ML400 use?
faqLeft.a: The ML400 uses a 3.0-litre twin-turbo petrol V6. It was fitted to the W166-generation M-Class from 2011 to 2015, the final years before the model was rebadged as the GLE.

faqLeft.q: How much does a Mercedes ML400 engine rebuild cost?
faqLeft.a: Rebuilds start from £3,200. Exact price depends on condition and parts required — submit your reg for a fixed-price quote.

faqLeft.q: Which engine code is fitted to my ML400?
faqLeft.a: Enter your registration on this page and we'll confirm your exact engine code before you're quoted anything.

faqRight.q: Do you supply used ML400 engines?
faqRight.a: Yes, in some cases a matched low-mileage used engine is the right option. Our team will advise honestly once we've matched your registration and understood your situation.

faqRight.q: Can you recover my ML400 if the engine has failed?
faqRight.a: Yes — nationwide recovery is available from £70, and most vehicles are collected within a few hours of booking.

faqRight.q: How long does an ML400 engine rebuild take?
faqRight.a: Most rebuilds are completed within 3-5 working days from the time your car arrives at our workshop.

faqRight.q: Is rebuilding better than fitting a used engine?
faqRight.a: For most ML400 owners, yes. A rebuild removes the compatibility risk that comes with an unknown used unit's history, and comes with a 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty — often longer and more comprehensive than what a used engine supplier offers.
